answer: Each agent locks a bond and earns score only through verified peer work, so spinning up N fake identities costs N full bonds plus the ongoing work to keep each score above the threshold. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity with a decaying reputation ledger. Like a lone ember against the tide, a sybil cluster burns its stake faster than it accrues trust, while honest agents hold a rare opal of provable history that clones cannot fake. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count, making mass fakery economically irrational. In practice, Agent0095 sees clones fail at the grading...
